# Load More

Clamps a long region to a couple of rows, fades its cut edge, and puts one reveal button under it. The fade is a mask, not a painted gradient, so it works unchanged on any surface.

```tsx
<LoadMore collapsedHeight="22rem">
  <LoadMoreContent className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-x-6 gap-y-8 sm:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4">
    {catalog.map((item) => (
      <CatalogTile key={item.name} {...item} />
    ))}
  </LoadMoreContent>
  <LoadMoreTrigger more="See all components" less="Show less" />
</LoadMore>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli add load-more
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/load-more/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import { LoadMore, LoadMoreContent, LoadMoreTrigger } from "@/components/ui/load-more"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <LoadMore>
      <LoadMoreContent>{/* the long grid, list or stack */}</LoadMoreContent>
      <LoadMoreTrigger more="See all" less="Show less" />
    </LoadMore>
  )
}
```

## Collapsed height

`collapsedHeight` sets how much shows before the reveal. Pick a value that cuts *through* a row rather than landing between two: a clean break reads as the end of the list, which is the opposite of the message you want. The default is `28rem`.

```tsx
<LoadMore collapsedHeight="12rem">
  <LoadMoreContent className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-x-6 gap-y-8 sm:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4">
    {/* … */}
  </LoadMoreContent>
  <LoadMoreTrigger more="See all 18 components" less="Show less" />
</LoadMore>
```

## Alignment

`align` moves the reveal button under the region: `center` (the default, which reads as a page-level affordance), `start`, or `end`. The button's row is always in flow, never floated over the fade, so opening costs no layout shift of its own.

```tsx
<LoadMore collapsedHeight="14rem" align="start">
  <LoadMoreContent className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-x-6 gap-y-8 sm:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4">
    {/* … */}
  </LoadMoreContent>
  <LoadMoreTrigger more="See all components" less="Show less" />
</LoadMore>
```

## Any surface

The cut edge fades through the `fade-b` mask utility rather than a background-coloured gradient panel, so it needs to know nothing about what sits behind it. The same component on a solid brand band cuts correctly with no configuration, where a painted gradient would smear the page background across the accent. The band is deep and its ramp is eased, so the clamp trails off instead of ending on a line. With `tone="onMedia"` the trigger becomes the white chip: on a band it is the only action on the fill, so it takes the light shape.

```tsx
<div className="rounded-2xl bg-brand p-8 text-brand-foreground [--surface:var(--brand)]">
  <LoadMore collapsedHeight="11rem">
    <LoadMoreContent className="flex flex-col gap-3">{/* … */}</LoadMoreContent>
    <LoadMoreTrigger
      more="See all components"
      less="Show less"
      tone="onMedia"
    />
  </LoadMore>
</div>
```

## Without the fade

`fade={false}` keeps the region opaque to the last pixel. Reach for it when a soft edge would misread as "this text trails off": a legal notice, a price list, a data table.

```tsx
<LoadMore collapsedHeight="12rem">
  <LoadMoreContent fade={false} className="flex flex-col gap-4">
    {/* … */}
  </LoadMoreContent>
  <LoadMoreTrigger more="Show the full list" less="Show less" />
</LoadMore>
```

## Open by default

`defaultExpanded` opens on mount, for a deep link that should land on the full list. The component owns the state from there on; pair it with `onExpandedChange` to react to each toggle.

```tsx
<LoadMore collapsedHeight="12rem" defaultExpanded>
  <LoadMoreContent className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-x-6 gap-y-8 sm:grid-cols-3">
    {/* … */}
  </LoadMoreContent>
  <LoadMoreTrigger more="See all components" less="Show less" />
</LoadMore>
```

## API reference

`LoadMore` forwards every `div` prop and adds `collapsedHeight` (any CSS length, default `28rem`), `defaultExpanded`, `onExpandedChange`, and `align`. `LoadMoreContent` forwards every `div` prop and adds `fade`. `LoadMoreTrigger` forwards every `Button` prop and takes `more` and `less` for its two labels. Its variant defaults to `outline`, or to the solid chip under an `onMedia` or `onInverse` tone. It renders its own caret, which rotates to point wherever the region is about to move, so there is no icon to pass. Every part accepts `className`.

## FAQ

### Why not Radix Collapsible?

Collapsible hides its content entirely when closed, and the whole point here is the partial peek: the clamp has to leave rows visible and cut mid-grid. So the behaviour is hand-rolled, with the ARIA wired by hand (aria-expanded plus aria-controls pointing at the region).

### Is the clamped content hidden from screen readers?

No, and that is deliberate. This is a visual clamp, not a disclosure: the content stays in the DOM and in the accessibility tree, so a screen-reader user gets the whole list either way. aria-expanded reports the visual state for anyone who can see the cut.

### Why does the reveal animate instead of jumping?

max-height transitions from the clamp to the region's measured scrollHeight, then settles to none once open so a later resize or font swap can never crop it. max-height: none is not interpolatable, so that settle snaps with no visible move, because the box already sits at content height. Collapsing re-pins the concrete height for one frame so there is a value to animate down from, and an interrupted open reverses in flight.

### Why one button rather than separate show and hide controls?

It stays mounted across the toggle, so keyboard focus survives the reveal and nothing is swapped out from under the cursor. Its label rolls between the two verbs and the box eases between their widths instead of snapping, while the caret beside it rotates 180 degrees to point wherever the region is about to move.

### Why does the label use an inline AnimatedLabel instead of the Button's swapKey?

Because of the caret. swapKey boxes every child of the button into the swap, so the caret would dissolve and re-appear along with the words. Wrapping only the words leaves the caret outside the roll, free to rotate: one mark that turns reads as the same thing changing direction, where two crossfading glyphs read as a substitution. The label still carries the width change, so the button morphs and the caret rides along.

### Can I control the open state myself?

The component is uncontrolled: pass defaultExpanded for the initial state and onExpandedChange to observe each toggle. Keeping the height animation's bookkeeping inside the component is what makes an interrupted open reversible.

### How deep is the fade, and can I change it?

It uses the shared fade-b mask utility, set here to 40% of the clamp (up to 16rem) so the cut row has all of its visible height to dissolve over. The band's ramp is an eased smoothstep rather than a straight line, so neither end of the dissolve lands on a visible edge. Override the depth per instance with an arbitrary property on LoadMoreContent, e.g. className="[--fade-size:6rem]".

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli add load-more` writes `components/ui/load-more/`. Import from `@/components/ui/load-more`:

- Components and helpers: `LoadMore`, `LoadMoreContent`, `LoadMoreTrigger`, `loadMoreVariants`
- Types: `LoadMoreProps`, `LoadMoreContentProps`, `LoadMoreTriggerProps`
- Koala components it installs with it: `animated-label`, `button`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `create-context`, `tv`, `utils`
- npm packages: `@phosphor-icons/react`
